key_insight: Hypersonic Couette flow and flat-plate boundary layers share near-wall SFS stress behaviour but differ in outer-layer and thermal dynamics, including a heat-flux sign change in the boundary layer.
engineering_relevance: SFS closures for hypersonic simulations should account for flow-dependent thermal structure and filter choice rather than assume universal stress and heat-flux behaviour.
method: Compare filtered DNS of both flows under strongly cooled-wall conditions.
Evaluate top-hat and sharp spectral filters.
Decompose SFS stresses and heat fluxes into resolved, residual and interaction contributions.
evidence_signal: Filtered DNS shows that residual contributions dominate mean SFS shear stress and heat flux, while resolved–residual interactions contribute with opposite signs in the two flows.
watch_item: The findings concern strongly cooled walls and are filter-sensitive; generalization to other thermal conditions requires validation.
paper_title: Sub-filter-scale stress and heat flux in hypersonic Couette flow and a flat-plate boundary layer
